name: Slippery Sam
description: Banking game: dealer puts up a stake; dealer deals three cards face-down to each player (players do not look), then turns cards face up until a six or lower appears; each player in turn bets on having a higher card of the same suit than that spot card; after betting, the hand is exposed and the player wins from or pays into the pot.

overview.description: Banking game: dealer puts up a stake; dealer deals three cards face-down to each player (players do not look), then turns cards face up until a six or lower appears; each player in turn bets on having a higher card of the same suit than that spot card; after betting, the hand is exposed and the player wins from or pays into the pot.

history.origins: Slippery Sam is a variant of Red Dog (also called High Card Pool), a banking game in which players bet on having a card of the same suit and higher rank than a card dealt from the pack. In Slippery Sam, also known as Six-Spot Red Dog, the dealer turns cards face up until a six or lower appears; players bet on that spot card without having seen their own hands. The card games literature varies on how the names Red Dog, Slippery Sam and Shoot are assigned to the different versions.
timeline: 20th century: Red Dog variant documented as Slippery Sam (Six-Spot Red Dog); players bet on dealer's turned card without seeing their hands.
1973: John Scarne's Encyclopedia of Games describes a Fort Wayne, Indiana variation with optional extra cards for a fee.

setup.players: Two or more players; one is dealer and banker each hand.
setup.dealing: Dealer deals three cards face-down to each other player; players must not look at their cards. Dealer then turns cards face up from the deck until a six or lower appears; that card is the spot card for the hand.
setup.equipment: Chips or money for the pot and bets.

rules.objective: Win money by betting that your hand contains a higher card of the same suit than the dealer's spot card (a six or lower); the dealer banks the pot and pays or collects each bet.
rules.gameplay: Dealer puts up a stake (the pot). Dealer deals three cards face-down to each other player; players must not look at their cards. Dealer then turns cards face up in the centre until a six or lower appears; that card is the spot card. In turn, each player bets an amount between an agreed minimum and the current pot that they hold a higher card of the same suit than the spot card. After the player bets, the player's hand is exposed. If it contains a higher card of the same suit, the player wins that stake from the pot; otherwise the bet is added to the pot. If the pot becomes empty during the hand, the deal passes to the next player who creates a new pot. At the end of the hand, the dealer keeps whatever remains in the pot and the deal passes to the next player.
keyRules: Six-spot: dealer turns cards until a six or lower appears; players bet on having a higher same-suit card.
Players do not look at their cards until after they have bet.
Bet between agreed minimum and current pot.

scoring.winCondition: Player wins stake from pot if hand contains a higher card of the same suit as the spot card; otherwise bet is added to pot. Dealer keeps remainder at end of hand.
